checks.name: parseval_energy
checks.reason: FFT->IFFT uses norm='ortho'; energy is preserved (Parseval/Plancherel).
refs: Parseval/Plancherel theorem — energy is preserved across an orthonormal Fourier transform (rfft2/irfft2 with norm='ortho').

checks.name: mode_truncation
checks.reason: Declared 'modes' is applied as a low-frequency truncation (FNO-style).
refs: Li et al. (2021), Fourier Neural Operator, arXiv:2010.08895 — spectral mixing keeps low Fourier modes and truncates high ones.

checks.name: gate_convex_sum
checks.reason: Softmax gate forms a convex combination, but the two summed paths must share shape/channels; an undefined op (e.g. placeholder wavelet_transform) makes shape equality unverifiable.
refs: Parseval/Plancherel theorem — energy is preserved across an orthonormal Fourier transform (rfft2/irfft2 with norm='ortho').

checks.name: definition_complete
checks.reason: Definition references 'wavelet_transform', which is not implemented. Shape/domain consistency cannot be proven for a not-yet-existing op.

checks.name: translation_symmetry
checks.reason: FFT mixing is translation-COVARIANT; full translation INVARIANCE must come from a downstream global pool (head 'gap+mlp'), not the layer itself. Consistent with Noether (symmetry -> conservation).
refs: Noether (1918) — every continuous symmetry implies a conserved quantity; translation symmetry <-> momentum conservation.

checks.name: energy_bound
checks.reason: A convex combination of two energy-bounded paths stays energy-bounded (weight sum = 1, non-negative). No unphysical energy gain.
refs: Noether (1918) — every continuous symmetry implies a conserved quantity; translation symmetry <-> momentum conservation.
Parseval/Plancherel theorem — energy is preserved across an orthonormal Fourier transform (rfft2/irfft2 with norm='ortho').

checks.name: domain_consistency
checks.reason: Combining an FFT-reconstructed spatial tensor with a wavelet output requires both in the same domain/shape. Placeholder wavelet op makes this unverifiable.
refs: Mallat (2012), Bruna & Mallat (2013) — wavelet scattering builds translation-invariant features via wavelet decompositions.

checks.name: landauer_forward
checks.reason: Forward pass performs no bit erasure; no Landauer heat floor applies to inference. Training updates dissipate per the Landauer bound, as for any model.
refs: Landauer (1961) — erasing one bit dissipates >= k_B*T*ln(2) heat; forward passes that do not erase bits incur no such floor.

checks.name: second_law
checks.reason: No claim of free-energy creation; the layer is a deterministic linear/learned map, consistent with the second law.
refs: Second law of thermodynamics — total entropy of a closed system never decreases; no process creates net free energy.

checks.name: novel_has_refs
checks.reason: Novel layer cites prior field research it builds on.

checks.name: claim_bounds
checks.reason: Hypothesis (improved sample efficiency) is a plausible inductive-bias claim, bounded by PAC-Bayes generalization limits; not a violation.
refs: McAllester (1999) PAC-Bayes; Shwartz-Ziv & Tishby (2017) — sample complexity is bounded; a better inductive bias lowers the bound but cannot beat information-theoretic limits.
